seo.title: Libas: full-funnel AI acquisition and retargeting (Criteo Commerce Growth) - +72% ROAS (2025)
seo.meta_description: How Libas, an Indian ethnic fast-fashion brand, entrusted its acquisition and retargeting to Criteo's AI: +72% ROAS and +133% conversion rate in one year.
seo.resume_citable: In 2025, the Indian fast-fashion brand Libas achieved +72% ROAS and +133% conversion rate year over year by entrusting its full-funnel acquisition and retargeting to the Criteo Commerce Growth AI platform (GO Campaigns and dynamic retargeting).

faq.a: The Criteo Commerce Growth platform: GO Campaigns for acquisition (ML-driven targeting and bidding) and dynamic retargeting for conversion, with no custom model on the brand side.

faq.q: Are the results attributed or incremental?
faq.a: Attributed: the figures rest on Criteo's 7-day click attribution, on a year-over-year comparison, not on an incremental test with a control group.

pattern: Full-funnel AI-driven acquisition and retargeting on a self-serve commerce media platform
objectif_business: Sustain a very fast catalog cadence (150 to 200 styles every two weeks) while keeping acquisition profitable: Criteo's AI chooses who to target and where to serve, the team focuses on product and budget.
description: Libas is an Indian fast-fashion brand in women's ethnic wear, which puts 150 to 200 new styles online every two weeks. This inventory pace creates an acquisition problem: each new collection has to find its buyers quickly, before it is replaced. The brand entrusted its paid distribution to Criteo's Commerce Growth platform, playing the whole funnel. For acquisition, it uses GO Campaigns, self-serve campaigns where Criteo's AI drives targeting and bidding to find new customers on the open internet and social networks. For conversion, it relies on dynamic retargeting, which re-shows visitors the products they viewed. On a year-over-year comparison (January 1 to December 12, 2024 versus the same period in 2025, Criteo 7-day click attribution), Libas reports +72% ROAS, +133% conversion rate, +108% CTR, for +104% ad spend. The partner Tyroo handled performance monitoring and optimization during the scale-up.

fonctionnement_operationnel.cadence: Continuous, daily budget, with renewal pressure tied to a catalog that changes every two weeks. Each wave of products has to be exposed quickly.
fonctionnement_operationnel.opere_par: Libas's marketing team, supported by the partner Tyroo for monitoring and optimization, on the Criteo self-serve platform.
fonctionnement_operationnel.signal_pilote: The site events (product views, add-to-cart, purchases) sent through the Criteo tag. If this feed is incomplete, retargeting re-shows the wrong products and acquisition optimizes on noise.

etapes.detail: The product catalog and site events go to Criteo. This feed powers both acquisition and retargeting.

etapes.etape: Launch the GO Campaigns for acquisition
etapes.detail: Self-serve campaigns where Criteo's AI chooses the audiences and bids to capture new buyers on the open internet and social.
Visitors see again the products they viewed, with recommendations computed by Criteo's engine. The heart of conversion for a fast-moving catalog.
The partner monitors ROAS and conversion, adjusting spend between acquisition and retargeting across the collection waves.

niveau_preuve.justification: A quantified Criteo case study, with the comparison period and attribution method specified (7-day click), but published by the platform itself (vendor bias). The same figures are picked up by the Indian trade press, which corroborates without removing the source bias: capped at B.

statut_vivant.note: Case study published in March 2026 on 2025 data. Libas remains an active advertiser and a growing brand (FY25 revenue around 609 crore rupees, +25% year over year, backed by ICICI Venture). Criteo Commerce Growth is a standard product on the platform.

transposable_ue.note: Criteo Commerce Growth is available in the EU. Retargeting and activation on the open internet assume GDPR/ePrivacy consent for the tag and the lists, plus a clean first-party data base. Algorithmic targeting remains a low risk under the AI Act on the advertiser side.
